In the high scenario, electricity prices are much higher, and savings potential is correspondingly about twice the low scenario. In 2019, savings potential would have been much more limited, especially on the mild tariff, due to lower penetration of flexible EV loads, lower electricity prices, and a less renewable grid that had more mild price differentials compared to the 2030 prices. EVs are the largest driver of potential bill savings, with space cooling coming in second. Crop irrigation and pool pumping loads are also significant, as their ability to save customers money year-round adds up. Savings from flexing residential water heating loads are also noticeable and are on par with commercial space cooling savings. Figure 22. As shown, the Full and medium tariffs tend to send more bill savings to customers than the system cost savings, calculated using the ACC, would imply they are worth. The mild tariff compensates customers 37 more on par with, though slightly lower than, estimated avoided costs. The extent to which this informs dynamic price design is dependent upon the representativeness of the avoided cost calculator avoided costs and the political initiatives of the dynamic price design. On one hand, it could be considered ideal for customers to be perfectly compensated for the value they create via system savings. Alternatively, savings may be designed to be slightly lower, such that the system savings can either be shared across multiple parties that have a hand in offering and maintaining the dynamic pricing infrastructure or be used to lower electricity costs for all customers, even those who may not have the ability to participate. The last option would be for customer bill savings to intentionally outweigh the system value, reducing the amount that customers pay when adjusting their load in response to price signals. This could be considered by some as overcompensation but does not deviate from traditional ratemaking practices that modulate what different types of customers, with different load characteristics, are charged for electricity. This type of design could help to grow a robust load flexibility ecosystem that could then generate substantial value. Figure 23.
